default.notes: A consular tourist visa is required — apply at a Chilean consulate before travel. Chile's exemption list is revised periodically, so confirm your status before booking.

groups.notes: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days. No arrival fee is charged. One extension of up to 90 further days can be bought from the Servicio Nacional de Migraciones before the stamp expires.

CL.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Chilean citizens.

AU.notes: Visa-free for 90 days. The reciprocity fee that Australians once paid on arrival at Santiago was abolished in 2020 — nothing is charged at the border.

VE.notes: Chile introduced a consular tourist visa requirement for Venezuelan citizens in 2019 and it remains in force — apply at a Chilean consulate, allowing extra time for processing.

HT.notes: Chile introduced a consular tourist visa requirement for Haitian citizens in 2018 — apply in advance at a Chilean consulate; approval is not routine.

CU.notes: Cuban citizens need a consular tourist visa for Chile; expect to document funds, accommodation and an onward ticket.

DO.notes: Dominican citizens have needed a consular tourist visa for Chile since 2012 — apply before travel.

CN.notes: Chinese citizens need a consular tourist visa; Chile has at times simplified processing for organised tour groups and for holders of valid US or Schengen visas — confirm current facilities with the consulate.

IN.notes: Indian citizens need a consular tourist visa for Chile — apply at a Chilean consulate well before travel.

TW.notes: Chile recognises the People's Republic of China; Taiwanese passport holders should confirm current handling with the Chilean commercial office, as treatment differs from that of PRC passports.

XK.notes: Chile does not recognise Kosovo, so Kosovan passports are not on the exemption list — apply for a consular visa, or travel on a second nationality if you hold one.
